slot.brief: Give an idiom like 'to let the cat out of the bag' in a mini-context; select the correct figurative meaning.

stem: The board introduced a new eligibility requirement after applicants had met its published criteria. Critics said it was ______.
options: making a mountain out of a molehill
letting the cat out of the bag

verdicts.working: Adding a new requirement after applicants met the published criteria means changing the rules after the fact—“moving the goalposts.”

working:
“Move the goalposts” means changing the rules or criteria while a process is under way.
The other idioms mean revealing a secret, shifting responsibility, and exaggerating a minor issue.

Independent check: Adding a new requirement after applicants met the published criteria means changing the rules after the fact—“moving the goalposts.”
solution: “Moving the goalposts” means changing the rules or criteria after a process has begun. Adding a new requirement after applicants met the published criteria fits this meaning.
